To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we introduce the first vision based model predictive controller that learns to actuate a pendulum system from vision alone, and (2) we propose the first unsupervised physical parameter estimation method from video that can learn to control the system from video alone, without requiring any explicit supervision on states or objects.

we propose a model that learns to estimate physical parameters from video without explicit supervision, and that this model is able to perform long term video prediction and data efficient vision based control.
we can perform long term video prediction and vision based model predictive controller learning of physical scenes without supervision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: can we learn interpretable models of physical systems and control them from video alone?

the question of whether it is possible for a model of a system to learn to predict its future behavior, without explicit supervision of its state, by learning to infer the parameters of its physical model from the observed dynamics of the system.
how to learn interpretable physics based scene representations from video, and how to use these representations for long term extrapolation and control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to perform long term future video prediction and control of systems with interacting bodies without supervision.
we present a novel approach to physics based scene understanding that is able to learn to predict the future and perform model based control in systems with interacting objects.
we propose a model that can estimate the physical parameters of a system from video and can be used for vision based model predictive controller for systems where the dynamics is known.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to learn interpretable physical models of systems from raw video data without any explicit state supervision.
we propose a model that can learn physical parameters of a system from video and use it to perform model based control.
we show how vision can be used to discover physical systems from raw video and use this knowledge to control the system in a data efficient way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
vision and physics can be integrated into a single model, which can then be used for long term extrapolation, and model based control.
physics as inverse graphics is an effective framework for unsupervised scene understanding and control.
the vision and physics models can be learned jointly to achieve a tight coupling that enables long term video prediction and data efficient model based control.
